# Verify a recipient can be given as a relative file:// path: the key file lives
# inside the repository so every admin resolves the same spec. Absolute file://
# paths are refused for exactly that reason.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

exec sesam init --user admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

# A relative file:// path is read through the repo root and recorded verbatim as
# the key's source in the audit log.
exec sesam tell --user peter --recipient file://keys/peter.pub --group dev
exec sesam show .sesam/audit/log.jsonl
stdout '"peter"'
stdout 'file://keys/peter.pub'

exec sesam verify

# An absolute file:// path is refused - other admins could not read it.
! exec sesam tell --user mallory --recipient file:///etc/hostname --group dev
stderr 'must be relative'

# A path escaping the repository via .. is confined by the repo root.
! exec sesam tell --user mallory --recipient file://../outside.pub --group dev

# Key files carry headers - age-keygen writes two of them - so comments are
# skipped rather than taken for key material.
exec sesam tell --user paula --recipient file://keys/paula.pub --group dev
exec sesam user list
stdout 'paula'

# Pointing at the age-keygen *identity* file instead of the public key is an
# easy mistake (it is the same file `sesam init -i` takes). It has to be named
# as such, and the private key must never be echoed back.
! exec sesam tell --user percy --recipient file://keys/percy.age --group dev
stderr 'private key'
! stderr 'AGE-SECRET-KEY'
! stdout 'AGE-SECRET-KEY'

# A file without any usable key fails on the spot, not somewhere downstream.
! exec sesam tell --user pam --recipient file://keys/pam.pub --group dev
stderr 'no public key'

exec sesam verify

-- keys/peter.pub --
age1gtfhwme5a3sg9r7sp9vqu5awdzft4xd5qjesdq8lhry5wy8tfsfqw7fgt6
-- keys/paula.pub --
# paula, laptop key
# created: 2026-09-13T14:00:52+02:00

age1dzsks48f0xuf59qma3mv5a9hxrq4yq5eymd0d4ajg74gu6xnj3dqc9j0rl
-- keys/percy.age --
# The payload is not a real key - only its prefix decides how sesam reads it.
# created: 2026-09-13T14:00:52+02:00
# public key: age1r95e9036u9hyt6cemhmecgk2vykha3w7jfv9g6n45295w9k0rvxql0nkp2
AGE-SECRET-KEY-1NOTAREALKEYNOTAREALKEYNOTAREALKEYNOTAREALKEYNOTAREALKEYXXXXX
-- keys/pam.pub --
# public key: age1r95e9036u9hyt6cemhmecgk2vykha3w7jfv9g6n45295w9k0rvxql0nkp2
